mechanism_narrative: The four-week monotonic improvement in RETAIL_REC from -42.9 to -38.6 reflects an ongoing reopening impulse; because the series has not reversed, its own momentum predicts a higher four-week mean over the next 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -42.9 at t-3w to -38.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT crossing above -40 percent change from baseline signals normalization of public-transport routines; because retail trips depend on transit access, RETAIL_REC should rise over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -40 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -42.1 at t-3w to -37.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: After TRANSIT crosses above -40, the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is not higher than over the preceding 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery in PARKS and TRANSIT indicates that out-of-home social routines are being restored; the interaction of outdoor activity and transit use raises RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -26.0 to -15.4 and TRANSIT rose from -42.1 to -37.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: When PARKS > -20 and TRANSIT > -40, the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than over the preceding 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES crossing above -25 percent change from baseline signals a return of office commuting, which increases weekday retail-and-recreation footfall within one week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -25 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -28.0 at t-3w to -24.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: In the week after WORKPLACES exceeds -25, RETAIL_REC is not higher than in the preceding week.

mechanism_narrative: Policy relaxation is evidenced by RESIDENTIAL falling below 23.0 and GROCERY_PHARM nearing its baseline; reduced stay-at-home constraints should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 24.3 to 22.6 and GROCERY_PHARM rose from -4.3 to -0.4
regime_hint: policy relaxation with declining residential mobility
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL is below 23.0 and GROCERY_PHARM is above -1.0, the next 28-day mean RETAIL_REC fails to exceed the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM normalization combined with TRANSIT recovery jointly signals restored consumer mobility confidence; the interaction predicts higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -4.3 to -0.4 and TRANSIT rose from -42.1 to -37.7
failure_condition: When GROCERY_PHARM > -2 and TRANSIT > -40, the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A seasonal shift toward outdoor activity, visible in PARKS rising from -26.0 to -15.4, pulls family-oriented retail-and-recreation upward over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -26.0 at t-3w to -15.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS remains above -20 for two consecutive weeks, RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not rise relative to the preceding 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL rises back above 24.0 percent change from baseline, renewed stay-at-home behavior will suppress retail-and-recreation mobility within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 24.0 percent change from baseline
